property_summary: For any caller and amount, if Collect succeeds then the caller's stored balance decreases by exactly the collected amount (balances(caller) after) = (balances(caller) before) - _am; the mutant that subtracts msg.value on Deposit breaks this invariant for some inputs because deposits can corrupt balances so Collect's effect on balances differs.

For any depositor and any deposit/collect amounts, if a caller deposits X (via Deposit) and later Collects amount Y (where caller had >= MinSum and >= Y), then after Collect the caller's recorded balance decreases by exactly Y; the mutant that subtracts msg.value on Deposit corrupts balances so there exists inputs where Collect does not reduce the caller's balances by Y.

For any depositor and collect amount where Collect is allowed, after Collect completes the reference contract's balances at every address never increases compared to before Collect (i.e., no address gains balance as a result of Collect), whereas the mutant can cause some address's balance to increase due to corrupted deposits, so this monotonic non-increase property is violated for some inputs.

For any caller, if Collect(_am) is permitted (caller balance >= MinSum and >= _am) then after Collect completes the caller's balances(caller) equals its pre-Collect balance minus _am; the mutant (which subtracts msg.value on Deposit) corrupts balances via Deposit and thus there exist inputs where this equality fails.

For any caller and any sequence of deposits and a Collect(_am) call that succeeds, the reference contract ensures that after Collect completes the total sum of all stored balances (sum over public balances mapping across observed addresses) decreases by exactly _am (i.e., Collect only removes funds); the mutant (which subtracts msg.value on Deposit) can corrupt balances so there exist inputs where the total stored sum changes differently and thus the property is violated.
After calling Deposit with a specified wei value, the sender's balance recorded in c.balances equals its previous recorded balance plus that wei value (allowing zero-value deposits).
